flashcard_questions.q: Which gas must be present along with water for iron to rust?
What is the chemical name for rust?
Why does rusting continue until all the iron has corroded?
flashcard_questions.a: Rust is soft and flaky, so it falls away and exposes fresh metal.

flashcard_questions.q: Which metal coats iron and steel in galvanising?
How does sacrificial protection stop iron corroding?
flashcard_questions.a: A more reactive metal oxidises instead, donating electrons to the iron.

flashcard_questions.q: What is an alloy in chemistry?
flashcard_questions.a: A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is an alloy harder than a pure metal?
flashcard_questions.a: Different-sized atoms disrupt the regular layers, so they cannot slide over each other.

flashcard_questions.q: Which element is mixed with iron to make steel?
In a composite material, what is the matrix?
flashcard_questions.a: The background material that binds everything together.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the balanced equation for the Haber process?
Which catalyst is used in the Haber process?
What temperature is used in the Haber process?
What pressure is used in the Haber process?
Why is 450 °C used in the Haber process rather than a lower temperature?
flashcard_questions.a: A lower temperature gives a higher yield but makes the reaction too slow.

flashcard_questions.q: Which plant growth does the nitrogen in an NPK fertiliser promote?
